item.title: Linux NTFS3 Driver Will Now Support Timestamps Prior To 1970
item.description: While NTFSPLUS continues to be developed as a new and modern NTFS open-source driver for Linux systems, at the moment NTFS3 from Paragon Software remains the most capable NTFS file-system driver within the mainline kernel. For the Linux 6.19 merge window a variety of fixes have landed for this driver...

item.title: Intel Graphics Score A Big Win With Linux 6.19: Color Management & Xe VFIO Driver Merged
item.description: On top of enabling Xe3P graphics for Nova Lake and Crescent Island plus other changes like CASF adaptive sharpening for Lunar Lake and newer, another set of Intel kernel graphics driver updates were merged overnight as a big win for the open-source Intel graphics stack on Linux...

item.title: Venus Vulkan Driver Lands Mesh Shader Support In Mesa 26.0
item.description: Venus is the VirtIO-GPU driver that allows for Vulkan support within guest virtual machines permitting sufficient host driver support and other requirements in place with hypervisors like CrosVM and QEMU. The Venus driver now supports Vulkan's mesh shader capabilities and in turn advances the DXVK-Proton support for Linux gaming within VMs...

item.title: Intel Updates Cache Aware Scheduling For Linux With Better NUMA Balancing
item.description: Intel engineer Tim Chen has sent out a second version of the proposed Cache Aware Scheduling patches for the Linux kernel to enhance the CPU performance of modern processors sporting multiple cache domains...

item.title: AMD EPYC 7773X "Milan-X" Performance & Power Nearly Four Years Later
item.description: Nearly four years have passed since AMD launched their EPYC Milan-X processors with 3D V-Cache. When recently rearranging some servers in the lab and realizing the four year anniversary was coming up in March, curiosity got the best of me in wondering where the Linux performance and energy efficiency on Milan-X is now with the latest Linux software stack compared to the numbers when Milan-X launched back in March 2022.

item.title: Jolla Trying Again To Develop A New Sailfish OS Linux Smartphone
item.description: Finnish company Jolla started out 14 years ago where Nokia left off with MeeGo and developed Sailfish OS as a new Linux smartphone platform. Jolla released their first smartphone in 2013 after crowdfunding but ultimately the Sailfish OS focus the past number of years now has been offering their software stack for use on other smartphone devices. But now it seems they are trying again with a new crowd-funded smartphone...

item.title: NVIDIA Improves Block Layer Peer-To-Peer DMA In Linux 6.19
item.description: The IO_uring and block subsystem changes have been merged for the Linux 6.19 merge window with a few improvements worth highlighting this cycle...

item.title: Linux Still Dealing With Quirky Firewire Devices As We Enter 2026
item.description: For Linux 6.19 as what will be the first stable kernel release of 2026, the IEEE-1394 Firewire stack continues dealing with device quirks and improving support for different Firewire-connected devices. In 2026 is also when the Linux Firewire maintainer plans to begin recommending users migrate away from the IEEE-1394 bus followed by closing the Linux Firewire efforts in 2029...

item.title: Wine 11.0-rc1 Released With TWAINDSM 64-bit Module For Scanners
item.description: As anticipated the first release candidate of Wine 11.0 is now available in working toward the annual stable release in January...

item.title: An Intel Fellow & Prominent Linux Performance Engineer Resigns From Intel
item.description: There have been many Intel Linux/open-source software engineers to leave the company over the past year among other setbacks for their Linux/open-source initiatives. Announced this Friday night is one of their highest profile departures of the year as it pertains to their Linux efforts...
